blocks.text: Debt can add income and diversification to a portfolio, but it brings credit, interest-rate, inflation, and liquidity risks. Compare products with your goals and time horizon.
When you buy a stock, you become an Owner (Risk). When you buy a Bond, you become a Lender (Safety).

Savings-account and deposit rates vary by institution, tenure, customer category, and date. Check current terms before comparing them with bonds.
The Hack: A G-Sec is a government borrowing instrument, but its market price can change before maturity. Compare its yield at your purchase price, maturity, liquidity, and risks with a deposit; the products are not interchangeable.
blocks.title: 🏦 The Indian Reality

blocks.text: A lender receives contractual interest and repayment terms, while an owner participates in uncertain business outcomes. Debt may rank ahead of equity in a default, but recovery is not guaranteed. Check who owes the money and what backs the obligation.
blocks.title: ⚖️ Lender’s Trade-Off

blocks.text: It is a loan you give to the Government or a Corporation.
Illustration: a ₹100 bond with a 7% annual coupon pays ₹7 per year if the issuer pays as promised

A bond’s key terms include issuer, face value, coupon, maturity, repayment priority, and any security or covenants. A stated coupon is not the same as your total return if you buy at a premium or discount, sell early, or face default.
blocks.title: 🧾 Bond Checklist

blocks.text: This is the hardest concept in finance, explained simply.
If Interest Rates go UP, Bond Prices go DOWN.

Suppose a bond pays a fixed 6% coupon and market yields for comparable bonds rise to about 8%.
All else equal, the bond’s market price may fall so its yield is more competitive. The actual price also depends on time to maturity, credit risk, and market conditions.
blocks.title: 📉 Example

blocks.text: Imagine an existing bond pays a fixed coupon while newly issued bonds begin offering higher rates. Buyers may require a lower price for the older bond to match the new yield. Longer-maturity bonds usually respond more to rate changes, all else equal.
blocks.title: 📉 Price and Yield Example

blocks.text:
Long Duration Funds (10 Year+ Bonds): These are highly sensitive to interest rates. Long-duration funds can be sensitive to interest-rate changes. Falling yields may lift bond prices and rising yields may reduce them; the result depends on the portfolio, timing, credit events, and your holding period.
Strategy: Choose a fund by matching its duration, credit quality, liquidity, and redemption terms to your needs. Neither a fund name nor a target maturity removes investment risk.
blocks.title: ☠️ GOD MODE: Duration Risk

blocks.text: Read the issuer’s financial position, rating rationale, security, seniority, and maturity. A credit rating is an opinion that can change; it is not a guarantee. Avoid concentrating money you may need soon in a single issuer or hard-to-sell instrument.
